resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Youth must meet HUD FYI/FUP youth criteria: age 18 through 24, left foster care or will leave foster care within 90 days, and homeless or at risk of homelessness. HUD states the public child-welfare agency refers eligible youth to the PHA, which then determines Housing Choice Voucher eligibility. Housing Connect announced 52 FYI vouchers for youth ages 18-24 who left or are transitioning from foster care and are homeless or at risk. Sources: https://housingconnect.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Press-Release-FYI-vouchers-2024_Redacted.pdf and https://www.hud.gov/helping-americans/housing-choice-vouchers-family

Renaissance Ranch describes full-service care for adult men, including medical detox, residential treatment, outpatient, and residential support homes. The site says it is now accepting Medicaid, but clinical admission criteria, insurance authorization, self-pay costs, medication policies, and bed availability must be confirmed. Call admissions at 855-736-7262 or email admissions@renaissanceranch.com. Ask specifically about Bluffdale residential treatment, detox, residential support homes, Medicaid/insurance acceptance, costs, and current openings.

resources.description: State disability-services pathway funding residential and in-home supports such as supported living, host homes, professional parent supports, adaptations, and support coordination through Medicaid waivers.
resources.hours: State office/intake hours not confirmed from reviewed pages; call DSPD for intake and eligibility instructions.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
DSPD services depend on which Medicaid waiver a person qualifies for. Residentially relevant services include host homes, professional parent supports, supported living, environmental adaptations, and support coordination. Formal disability eligibility, Medicaid waiver enrollment, assessment, documents, and waitlist timing must be confirmed through DSPD. Source: https://dspd.utah.gov/services/

**How to Best Connect**
Call DSPD at 801-538-4200 or toll-free 844-275-3773 to ask for intake and eligibility screening, waiver status, waiting-list information, and provider options in Salt Lake County.

**Access**
DSPD is statewide and serves eligible Utah residents, including Salt Lake County. Supported living helps people live independently in their own homes, with roommates, or with a spouse; host homes and professional parent supports can provide out-of-home placements in trained family/private-home settings.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency housing and does not guarantee an apartment. Supports depend on eligibility, waiver funding, assessed need, provider capacity, and possible waiting lists. Confirm current rules before making housing plans.
resources.name: Utah DSPD - Residential Supports and Supported Living

West Valley City homeowners may qualify for home rehabilitation loans; resident owners of mobile homes may qualify for mobile home repair grants; and extremely low-income homeowners may qualify for emergency repair grants to prevent further damage. **Eligibility Requirements**
Fortitude Treatment Center is designed to serve male parolees. Utah Department of Corrections says it serves as a transition facility for people released from prison who do not have appropriate housing arranged before parole, and as a stabilization facility for structured reentry planning. Source: https://corrections.utah.gov/inmate-services/reentry-and-rehabilitation/community-correctional-centers/fortitude-treatment-center/

Placement is through Utah Department of Corrections and Adult Probation and Parole. Eligible people should work with their institutional case manager or AP&P agent; the public cannot apply independently. Facility phone is 801-886-7800 for official program questions.

The facility is at 1747 S 900 W in Salt Lake City. Residents are subject to stricter restrictions than ordinary community supervision and are expected to find employment, attend recommended treatment, follow center rules, and work with a case manager.

This is correctional reentry housing/stabilization, not a shelter, rental program, or treatment bed open to the public. Admission depends on parole status, DOC/AP&P decisions, program need, and available space.
resources.name: Utah Department of Corrections - Fortitude Treatment Center

resources.address: 850 W 1700 S, Suite 1, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: No-cost home weatherization audits and energy-efficiency repairs for eligible households in Salt Lake, Tooele, Davis, Weber, and Morgan counties, with crisis weatherization for qualifying homeowners.
resources.hours: Utah Community Action intake line Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; exact Weatherization office walk-in hours are not posted. Drop boxes are available outside at 850 W 1700 S, Suite 1.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Homeowners or renters may qualify when the computerized energy audit shows a clear need and household income is at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. UCA gives precedence to elderly and disabled households and households with children under age six. Required documents include Social Security cards or a HEAT approval letter, bill-history release authorization and utility bill copy, declaration and proof of ownership or owner approval, and income verification if not on HEAT. Renters need owner approval. Source: https://utahca.org/home-weatherization/

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online from UCA's Weatherization page or call 801-359-2444 for help. Completed applications and documents may be faxed to 801-214-3208, mailed to Utah Community Action Weatherization Program, 850 W 1700 S Suite 1, Salt Lake City, UT 84104, dropped in the outside drop boxes at the same address, or submitted as instructed on the application page. Weatherization email: weatherization@utahca.org.

**Access**
UCA's intake line is posted as Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM. The Weatherization program serves Salt Lake, Tooele, Davis, Weber, and Morgan counties. Services may include home inspection, computerized energy audit, energy education, lighting replacement, furnace/window/door repairs, carbon monoxide testing, and insulation. Crisis services are available for homeowners with no heat in winter, no air conditioning in summer, or a broken water heater; UCA says crisis applicants must be the homeowner, currently on HEAT, and the HEAT and Weatherization applications must be under the same U.S. citizen household member's name.

**Important Information to Know**
Weatherization is not a general remodel or home-rehabilitation program; painting, roof repairs, siding replacement, and most capital-value improvements are not covered. UCA says applicants should receive an approval verification letter within two weeks after a complete application, but non-crisis work may take several months or longer until the applicant reaches the top of the priority list. Sources: https://utahca.org/home-weatherization/ and https://utahca.org/get-help/
resources.name: Utah Community Action - Weatherization Assistance Program

resources.address: Mobile service in northern Utah, including Salt Lake County; no fixed public overnight shelter address posted
resources.description: Peer-run mobile Blue Bus shelter and resource access for unsheltered people in northern Utah during the coldest part of winter, with limited capacity and variable locations.
resources.hours: Seasonal winter service during the coldest part of winter; exact nightly schedule, location, and intake hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Nomad Alliance describes itself as serving chronically unsheltered people in Salt Lake County and northern Utah. Public pages do not post formal documentation requirements, referral requirements, or disability-access rules for sleeping on the Blue Bus. The Blue Bus page says no drug use is allowed inside or near the bus. Sources: https://www.nomadalliance.org/ and https://www.nomadalliance.org/bluebus

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Nomad Alliance before relying on the bus for a specific night because the Blue Bus is mobile and public nightly location details are not posted. Nomad Alliance's current site lists 801-688-3197 and info@nomadalliance.org; the Blue Bus page footer also lists 801-200-3573. For ordinary Salt Lake County shelter placement, also use the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999.

**Access**
Nomad Alliance says the Blue Bus runs during the coldest part of winter and has housed 10-24 people every winter night for multiple seasons while also providing daytime supports such as water, ID vouchers, naps, phone charging, Wi-Fi, hot meals, and lockers. A January 24, 2026 Nomad Alliance media advisory says the upgraded bus includes shower and bathroom features, solar power, and interior renovations. Exact seasonal start and end dates, nightly hours, pickup/location process, ADA accessibility, and capacity for a given night are unconfirmed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a small, grassroots, peer-run mobile shelter and resource model, not a licensed fixed-site shelter with guaranteed beds. No participant fee was found in reviewed public materials, but availability, rules, location, and accessibility must be confirmed directly each season. Sources: https://www.nomadalliance.org/bluebus and https://www.nomadalliance.org/post/media-advisory-nomad-alliance-re-launches-nation-s-first-mobile-shelter-the-upgraded-blue-bus
resources.name: Nomad Alliance - Blue Bus Mobile Shelter

resources.address: 548 S 700 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Operational non-congregate microshelter community in Salt Lake City with hard-shell pods, shared hygiene facilities, meals, and case management; referral required through coordinated shelter access.
resources.hours: Utah 211 lists service hours as 24/7 for residents; referral/placement is through the homeless services coordinated entry line, and public walk-in intake is not advertised.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah 211 lists the Salt Lake Microshelter Community as serving unsheltered adults, minimum age 18. It says no substance use, weapons, or alcohol are allowed on site and that a referral is required from the coordinated entry line; callers should ask for specific eligibility criteria. Source: https://utahdhhs.211utah.org/node/354752

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999 for emergency shelter options and referral/placement. Shelter the Homeless says the hotline connects Salt Lake County residents experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness with emergency shelter options and community resources. Sources: https://homelessutah.org/contact-us/ and https://www.slc.gov/homelessservicesdashboard-3/

**Access**
The operational site is at 548 S 700 W in Salt Lake City. Switchpoint's page describes 50 hard-shell pods with power outlets, heating and AC, lockable doors, individualized case management, two meals per day for residents, community bathrooms and showers, and a community garden. Utah 211 lists 24/7 service hours, no cost, stays up to 120 days with possible 30-day extensions after case-management review, and couples permitted but housed in separate units. The program is often at capacity and Switchpoint notes a waiting list.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-up shelter and does not guarantee an immediate pod. The Utah Office of Homeless Services says Phase II opened September 28, 2024 at the state-owned 548 S 700 W site after the pilot became a permanent program with Switchpoint; later state materials describe the site as operating 50 units, with Phase 3 expansion paused because of funding reallocations. Confirm current waitlist, pets, couple rules, accessibility, and placement route through the hotline. Sources: https://switchpoint.org/where-we-are/locations/salt-lake/microshelter, https://jobs.utah.gov/department/press/2024/093024.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/homelessness/hex.pdf, and https://le.utah.gov/interim/2026/pdf/00002346.pdf
resources.name: Switchpoint - Salt Lake Microshelter Community

resources.description: Residential homes, supervised apartments, supported living, and Hub affordable housing connections for people with intellectual and/or physical disabilities in Salt Lake County.
resources.hours: Residential program office hours not posted on official pages; contact Columbus Community Center during business hours to confirm intake availability.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Columbus says its residential programs provide housing and support services for individuals with intellectual and/or physical disabilities. The Residential Services page says clients must first secure funding unless self-paying. Funding may come through DSPD, Vocational Rehabilitation, Medicaid, or private pay, depending on what the person qualifies for. Source: https://www.columbusserves.org/residential-services/ and https://www.columbusserves.org/funding-sources/

**How to Best Connect**
Call Columbus Community Center Residential Programs at 801-262-1552 or use the contact form on the Columbus site. Ask whether the person needs an existing DSPD budget or Medicaid waiver, whether private-pay openings exist, which residential model fits the person's support needs, current waitlists, and whether Hub apartment leasing must be handled separately through Housing Connect Property Management at 801-270-1337 or thehub@housingconnect.com. Sources: https://www.columbusserves.org/contact-us/ and https://www.columbusserves.org/

**Access**
Columbus lists residential sites at Park Creek, Foothill, Jones Court in Murray, Wren Road, The HUB in South Salt Lake, and Connor Street. Residential Homes provide family-style living and round-the-clock care for people with medical conditions or specialized support needs. Supervised Apartments support independence with structured daily-living supervision. Supported Living provides one-on-one hourly supports in a person's home. The Hub provides accessible affordable housing units and community living for individuals with disabilities. Public pages do not post office hours or vacancy status.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency homeless shelter. Access depends on disability-service eligibility, funding source, provider capacity, and housing availability. Columbus notes a DSPD waiting list can apply, while immediate needs may be considered during DSPD eligibility review. Hub apartments are affordable housing, not automatically free, and property-management leasing should be confirmed separately. Sources: https://www.columbusserves.org/residential-services/, https://www.columbusserves.org/funding-sources/, and https://www.columbusserves.org/
resources.name: Columbus Community Center - Residential Services and The HUB of Opportunity

resources.address: First United Methodist Church, 203 S 200 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; St. Mark's Cathedral, 231 E 100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Code Blue emergency winter shelter operated by Unsheltered Utah's 2nd + 2nd Coalition at downtown Salt Lake City churches on the coldest nights.
resources.hours: Only during Code Blue winter weather activations; nightly opening hours and capacity are not posted and should be confirmed before arrival.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves individuals experiencing homelessness during Code Blue weather events. Public materials reviewed did not post document requirements, ID requirements, age limits, pet policies, or exclusion rules. Salt Lake County Emergency Management says a Code Blue alert in Salt Lake County is issued when temperatures, including wind chill, are forecast to drop to 18 degrees Fahrenheit or below for two or more hours within a 24-hour period. Sources: https://unshelteredutah.org/ and https://saltlakecountyem.gov/be-prepared-community-outreach/extreme-weather/

**How to Best Connect**
For nightly activation and bed/shelter availability, call the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999. Unsheltered Utah public materials list admin@unshelteredutah.org and info@unshelteredutah.org for organization contact, but no dedicated public shelter-intake phone was verified.

**Access**
Unsheltered Utah says it leads the 2nd + 2nd Coalition, a group of Salt Lake County nonprofits, churches, and businesses that welcomes people into emergency winter shelters or movie nights on the coldest nights. Utah Legislature 2026 materials identify the hosts as First United Methodist Church and St. Mark's Cathedral in Salt Lake City and describe warm beds, hot meals, essential supplies, and wraparound support during Code Blue events. First United Methodist Church's official site lists 203 S 200 E; St. Mark's Cathedral is at 231 E 100 S. Exact nightly hours, entry process, and capacity are variable and unconfirmed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an emergency winter overflow/warming shelter model, not year-round housing and not guaranteed shelter every night. It operates only when activated for severe cold, and capacity can be limited. Confirm current Code Blue status and location before traveling. Sources: https://unshelteredutah.org/, https://unshelteredutah.org/our-efforts/, https://le.utah.gov/interim/2026/pdf/00002346.pdf, https://www.fumcslc.org/visit-us, and https://stmarksutah.org/
resources.name: Unsheltered Utah - 2nd + 2nd Coalition Code Blue Emergency Winter Shelter

resources.address: 80 S Orange St, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah Department of Corrections women-specific community correctional center providing four-to-six-month transitional reentry housing, treatment, classes, and living-plan support for women on parole.
resources.hours: 24-hour correctional residential facility; public intake hours do not apply because placement is through Utah DOC and Adult Probation and Parole.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah Department of Corrections says the Orange Street Women's Center houses 60 women who are being paroled and are in a transitional phase of community re-entry. This is for women in the Utah corrections/parole system, not people seeking public emergency shelter. Source: https://corrections.utah.gov/inmate-services/reentry-and-rehabilitation/community-correctional-centers/orange-street-community-correctional-center/

**How to Best Connect**
Placement is controlled by Utah Department of Corrections and Adult Probation and Parole. Eligible women should work with their institutional case manager, parole agent, or correctional reentry team. Facility phone is 801-596-6300; Women's Treatment Resource Center phone is 801-596-6311 for official program questions.

**Access**
The facility is at 80 S Orange Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84116. UDC describes a four-month to six-month stay with gender-responsive and strength-based staff interactions. The program includes clinical treatment, cognitive/behavioral/psycho-educational classes, community involvement, pro-social activities, and planning toward a living-wage job, positive community supports, and a foundational living plan. It is a structured correctional residential program with 24-hour facility operation rather than public walk-in access.

**Important Information to Know**
This is correctional transitional housing and treatment support, not rent help, shelter, or voluntary sober living. Admission depends on parole status, DOC/AP&P placement decisions, program fit, and available space. Current public materials confirm a 60-woman capacity, but real-time availability is not posted. Source: https://corrections.utah.gov/inmate-services/reentry-and-rehabilitation/community-correctional-centers/orange-street-community-correctional-center/
resources.name: Utah Department of Corrections - Orange Street Community Correctional Center

Spy Hop serves young people through media arts programming. Use the current in-house program or specific class page to register when registration is open, or call 801-532-7500 to ask about current apprenticeships, capstone classes, and waitlists. Source: https://spyhop.org/in-house-programs/

Programs are based at the Kahlert Youth Media Arts Center, 208 W Harvey Milk Blvd in Salt Lake City. Class days, times, registration windows, drop-in options, and apprenticeship schedules vary by term, so confirm the current calendar before referral.

Spy Hop describes in-house programs as free. Apprenticeships and advanced opportunities are selective and not guaranteed employment; confirm current stipend/payment, attendance requirements, transportation supports, and equipment access for the specific track.

resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Hire Heroes USA serves transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses. Clients register for no-cost personalized career services and work with a career advisor; job-board and advising access depends on completing intake. Source: https://www.hireheroesusa.org/what-to-expect/

**How to Best Connect**
Register through the Hire Heroes USA job-seeker page or call 844-634-1520. After intake, ask about resume help, cover letters, interview preparation, job-search strategy, training partners, and job-board access. Source: https://www.hireheroesusa.org/what-to-expect/

**Access**
Services are national and remote, so eligible Salt Lake County residents can participate without a Utah office. Appointment timing and communication method are arranged after registration.

**Important Information to Know**
Hire Heroes USA states it is not a placement agency; it provides guidance, tools, industry connections, and one-on-one support. Employment is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Hire Heroes USA - Veteran and Military Spouse Career Services

resources.hours: Online job search is available anytime; branch hours and walk-in availability were not confirmed on official pages, so call before visiting.

Applicants must meet requirements for specific manufacturing, factory, warehouse, or logistics assignments. Requirements may include shift availability, experience, transportation, work authorization, and employer screening. Sources: https://www.resourcemfg.com/locations/ and https://www.prologistix.com/locations/

Search and apply through the official ResourceMFG or ProLogistix job pages, or call the Salt Lake City/West Valley branch at 801-265-1999 to confirm current openings and whether walk-ins are accepted. Sources: https://www.resourcemfg.com/jobs/ and https://www.prologistix.com/jobs/

The official location lists include Salt Lake City, Utah branches. Third-party mapping corroborates a West Valley City ResourceMFG/ProLogistix location, but suite formatting and walk-in hours should be confirmed directly before visiting.

Staffing services are generally free to applicants, but jobs change quickly and employment is not guaranteed. Confirm pay, schedule, jobsite, assignment length, background/drug-screen rules, and whether a role is temporary, temp-to-hire, or direct hire.
resources.name: Employbridge - ResourceMFG and ProLogistix West Valley Staffing

resources.hours: National remote support; contact the WWP Resource Center for current intake and appointment availability.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Warriors to Work serves registered Wounded Warrior Project warriors and eligible family support members. Family members must be registered with WWP and age 18 or older for program support. Source: https://www.woundedwarriorproject.org/programs/warriors-to-work

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the WWP Resource Center at 888-997-2586 or use the Warriors to Work page to begin registration and request career support. Source: https://www.woundedwarriorproject.org/programs/warriors-to-work

Services are national and can be delivered by phone/online; no Salt Lake County office was verified. Appointment timing depends on WWP registration, eligibility, and staff scheduling.

The program includes career counseling, resume writing, interview preparation, salary negotiation tools, goal setting, military-skills translation, and networking opportunities. It is no-cost, but job placement is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Wounded Warrior Project - Warriors to Work

resources.description: State Certified Peer Support Specialist training and certification pathway for people with lived recovery experience seeking peer-support roles in Utah behavioral health settings.
resources.hours: Training cohorts and application windows vary by approved provider; contact Utah Peer Support or check the state page for current schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah's CPSS pathway is for people who use lived experience in recovery from mental health and/or substance use disorder to support others. The Youth and Young Adult peer support track is for ages 18-30 with lived experience. Applicants must use the current online application and meet state/provider requirements. Source: https://sumh.utah.gov/education/certification/peersupportspecialists/

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Utah DHHS Office of Substance Use and Mental Health peer-support page to apply online for CPSS certification or email the Utah Peer Support Program with questions. Source: https://sumh.utah.gov/education/certification/peersupportspecialists/

**Access**
This is a statewide certification pathway. Trainings may be in person, hybrid, or virtual through approved providers, including Salt Lake-area options such as USARA in Salt Lake City, UAPSS in South Salt Lake, and Optum in Draper. Cohorts and locations change.

**Important Information to Know**
The training builds skills for peer-support work, but certification does not guarantee employment. Employers may require additional background checks, supervision, continuing education, or job-specific qualifications.
resources.name: Utah DHHS OSUMH - Certified Peer Support Specialist Training and Certification

Applicants generally must meet apprenticeship requirements and obtain or pursue employment with a signatory contractor to be indentured. Sponsor-letter, document, and trade-specific requirements should be confirmed with the training center. Sources: https://www.wsctf.org/centers/utah/ and https://www.wsctf.org/apprenticeship/

Contact the Utah Training Center at 801-282-6535 or the local union office at 801-280-0292 to ask about applications, contractor sponsorship, pre-apprenticeship, and current openings. Source: https://www.wsctf.org/centers/utah/

Training is based at the West Jordan Utah Training Center. Apprentices work on contractor job sites and attend related instruction; class timing and openings depend on trade and employer demand.

This is an earn-while-you-learn apprenticeship path, not guaranteed immediate employment. Confirm current wages, fees/dues, tools, transportation expectations, dispatch process, and sponsor requirements directly with the training center or local.
resources.name: Western States Carpenters Training Fund - Utah Apprenticeship and Pre-Apprenticeship

resources.description: Adult English instruction for Utah residents, including intensive, flexible, citizenship, parent, and workplace English options that support job retention and employability.
resources.hours: Intensive track currently lists Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-12:30 PM or 12:30 PM-3:00 PM, with no evening classes; flexible and workplace schedules vary.
resources.informationText:

ESLC classes are only for people who live in Utah. Workplace training is limited to employees of partner companies. Class level, track, and enrollment availability should be confirmed during intake. Source: https://www.eslcenter.org/learn

**How to Best Connect**
Use the ESLC enrollment page, email info@eslcenter.org, or call 801-328-5608 to ask about eligibility, placement, current class openings, and nearby community class locations. Source: https://www.eslcenter.org/learn

**Access**

Apply for the state job at https://statejobs.utah.gov/, then email the recruitment number, job title, and disability documentation to asap@utah.gov. Job seekers generally need to qualify for Vocational Rehabilitation: a significant physical or mental impairment, a substantial impediment to employment, a need for VR services to obtain or maintain employment, and an expected employment benefit. Bring disability records if available, identification, Social Security card, and a completed VR application to a VR appointment. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/employer/choose.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/apply.html

**How to Best Connect**
For Choose to Work, contact Leah Lobato, Coordinator, at 801-887-9538 or leahlobato@utah.gov. Job seekers should also start through USOR Vocational Rehabilitation by calling 1-866-454-8397, contacting a local VR office, attending a welcome session, and completing a VR application. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/employer/choose.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/apply.html

**Access**

VR applications are handled through local VR offices, and a counselor has up to 60 days from appointment to determine eligibility unless more information is needed. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/apply.html

**Important Information to Know**
Choose to Work is no-cost and provides preparation and placement services to job seekers with disabilities while also supporting employers with recruiting, hiring, and retention. USOR VR is operating under an Order of Selection; newly eligible people in closed priority categories may be delayed and may receive only information and referral until their category opens. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/employer/choose.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/services/order.html

resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
DSBVI serves Utah residents who are blind or visually impaired. DSBVI VR serves people who are legally blind and certain qualifying people with significant visual impairments. TAS students must meet physical and mental requirements and be free from barriers that would impede attendance or progress. BEP requires legal blindness, age 18 or older, U.S. citizenship, Utah residency for at least one year, and passing an entry exam, site review, and initial interview. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/casemanagement.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/bep.html

**How to Best Connect**
Call the DSBVI Administrative Office at 801-323-4343 or 800-284-1823 if unsure which office serves you. To apply for VR, use the main USOR VR application process or drop an application at a USOR or DSBVI office. For TAS information, call Jodi Duke at 801-323-4348 or Adam Rushforth at 801-323-4347. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/contact.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/casemanagement.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html

**Access**
The Salt Lake administrative office and TAS classes are at 250 N 1950 W, Suite B, Salt Lake City. TAS classes are offered Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM and are taught at the Salt Lake site. VR services are statewide through DSBVI offices and local VR application processes. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/contact.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html

**Important Information to Know**
TAS is no cost to students and includes cane travel, Braille literacy, adaptive technology/computers, home management, and employment readiness. resources.description: University of Utah Tanner Dance disability programs including LEADD adult arts education, Elevate Theatre Company, adaptive needs dance classes, wheels dance, and related art/performance classes.
resources.hours: Class schedules vary by program; examples include LEADD Monday-Thursday 12:30 PM-3:30 PM, Elevate Saturdays 9:00 AM-11:30 AM, and adaptive dance classes on posted weekday/Saturday times.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Programs serve dancers with disabilities. LEADD is for adults with physical and/or intellectual disabilities who have aged out of the public school system; Elevate is for performers with disabilities; adaptive needs dance classes are for children and young adults with disabilities. LEADD and Elevate require a meeting/interview before registration. Source: https://tannerdance.utah.edu/dancers-with-disabilities/

**How to Best Connect**
For LEADD and Elevate, email Ben Tillotson at ben.tillotson@utah.edu to schedule a meeting before registration. For DSPD billing, Tanner Dance instructs families not to register online and to contact Sarah Cardenas at s.cardenas@utah.edu with the support coordinator's name, phone, and email. Source: https://tannerdance.utah.edu/dancers-with-disabilities/

**Access**
Programs are held at the University of Utah Tanner Dance site in Salt Lake City. Posted examples for 2026-2027 include LEADD classes Monday-Thursday 12:30 PM-3:30 PM, Elevate Theatre Company Saturdays 9:00 AM-11:30 AM, and adaptive dance/art classes at posted weekday or Saturday times.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a free program. The 2026-2027 catalog lists many LEADD/Elevate classes at $1,224 and adaptive dance classes around $710-$730, with a lower-cost InteGreat session listed separately. Scholarships and DSPD billing may help but are not guaranteed; parking, class fit, support needs, and registration availability should be confirmed.
resources.name: University of Utah Tanner Dance - Dancers with Disabilities Programs

resources.description: Long-Term Care Ombudsman advocacy contact for Salt Lake County residents of nursing homes, assisted living, and other covered long-term care facilities.
resources.hours: Ombudsman line hours were not posted on the reviewed page; call and leave a message if needed.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Ombudsman program helps with concerns involving long-term care facility residents. The Salt Lake contact is county-based; people should use the county where the facility/resident is located. Source: https://daas.utah.gov/ombudsman-locations-3/

**How to Best Connect**
For Salt Lake County, call the Ombudsman Line at 385-468-3255 or email ombudsman@slco.org. If concerns are not addressed or further help is needed, the state ombudsman contact is listed on the DHHS locations page. Source: https://daas.utah.gov/ombudsman-locations-3/

**Access**
The Salt Lake Ombudsman serves Salt Lake County facilities. Hours and response times were not posted, so callers should leave clear contact information, facility name, resident concern, and urgency if voicemail is reached.

**Important Information to Know**
This is rights advocacy and complaint help for facility residents, not emergency response, independent-living case management, or legal representation. For immediate danger, use emergency or protective-service channels.
resources.name: Utah Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program - Salt Lake County

resources.address: 195 N 1950 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah Medicaid HCBS Community Transitions Waiver helping people with intellectual disabilities or related conditions transition from ICF settings into community living with assessed supports.
resources.hours: State waiver office hours not posted; contact the transition program manager or DSPD/Medicaid for current referral steps.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Community Transitions Waiver requires ICF level of care, qualifying onset before age 18 for intellectual disability or before age 22 for related conditions, functional impairment in three or more major life areas, and Medicaid financial eligibility. It is designed for transition out of an Intermediate Care Facility for people with intellectual disabilities into community settings. Source: https://medicaid.utah.gov/ltc-2/community-transitions-home/

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the listed Transition Program Manager, Glen Larsen, at 385-303-8593 or glenlarsen@utah.gov, and ask about eligibility, referral, ICF transition planning, Medicaid requirements, and available waiver capacity. Source: https://medicaid.utah.gov/ltc-2/community-transitions-home/

**Access**
The waiver is statewide, including Salt Lake County. Services are limited to assessed needs and can include behavioral consultation, community transition services, day supports, environmental adaptations, extended living supports, homemaker, nursing, personal assistance, residential habilitation, respite, supported employment, supported living, and waiver support coordination. DSPD's Self-Administered Services model may be an option for eligible in-home supports when a fiscal agent is used. Source: https://dspd.utah.gov/services/service-delivery/

**Important Information to Know**
The number served depends on funding, and services are not automatic. Self-Administered Services is not a separate public program for people who are not waiver eligible; it is a way eligible people/families can hire and supervise some supports with fiscal-agent payroll/background-check help. Confirm current slots, facility-transition eligibility, and service-delivery options.
resources.name: Utah Medicaid and DSPD - Community Transitions Waiver

Spectrum Academy describes itself as a Utah charter school for students with autism and other neurodiversities who would benefit from its learning environment. Charter enrollment/lottery requirements, grade availability, diagnosis/IEP expectations, and deadlines should be confirmed through the school's enrollment page. Use Spectrum Academy's enrollment page or call the main number, 801-936-0318, to ask about campus options, lottery/deadlines, waitlists, transportation, IEP/504 services, and whether a diagnosis is required for the current admissions cycle. Source: https://www.spectrumcharter.org/

**Access**
Spectrum Academy lists North Salt Lake and Pleasant Grove campuses and says it serves students from across Utah's Wasatch Front. Campuses are outside Salt Lake County, so families should confirm transportation, commute feasibility, and campus assignment.

The school is tuition-free as a public charter, but admission is not guaranteed and depends on charter enrollment rules and available seats. Related services and accommodations depend on school evaluation and student plans; verify current program fit before leaving an existing placement.
resources.name: Spectrum Academy - Neurodiverse Public Charter School

resources.description: University of Utah Health interdisciplinary amputee rehabilitation and prosthetics program offering medical rehabilitation, therapy, prosthetic fitting/training, pain management, counseling, education, and community-resource information.

resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The program treats people with limb loss or limb difference, including leg, foot, finger, hand, arm, and multiple-limb amputations. Clinical eligibility, referral requirements, insurance authorization, and appointment availability must be confirmed with University of Utah Health. Source: https://healthcare.utah.edu/neilsen-physical-rehab-hospital/specialties/amputee

**How to Best Connect**
Use the University of Utah Health patient referral/contact path or call 801-646-8000 to ask about amputee program scheduling. For therapy-service routing, the submitted Salt Lake contact was 801-581-2221; confirm the correct clinic before going.

**Access**
Services are local to University of Utah Health/Craig H. Neilsen Rehabilitation Hospital and related therapy sites. Appointments are scheduled; this is not a drop-in support group or equipment giveaway.

The program includes rehabilitation physicians, physical and occupational therapists, prosthetists, surgeons, nurses, social workers, rehabilitation psychologists, prosthetic limb fitting, pain management, and education. Costs depend on insurance and clinical authorization. Any monthly amputee support group date/location should be confirmed separately before attending.
resources.name: University of Utah Health - Amputee Program

resources.description: Huntington's Disease Society of America Utah Chapter support, education, social-work/resource navigation, support groups, and connection to University of Utah HD specialty care.
resources.hours: Chapter and support-group schedules vary; national helpline and clinic appointment hours should be confirmed when calling.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
HDSA Utah Chapter resources are for people and families impacted by Huntington's disease, including loved ones and at-risk relatives. Clinic eligibility, genetic testing, referral, and insurance requirements must be handled through medical providers. Source: https://utah.hdsa.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Use the HDSA Utah Chapter website to find current events and support groups, call the HDSA helpline at 800-345-HDSA (4372), or use HDSA's resource locator. For University of Utah clinic care, call the clinic contact directly and confirm referral/insurance needs. Source: https://utah.hdsa.org/

**Access**
The Utah Chapter posts Salt Lake City events and identifies HDSA support groups as free for individuals, loved ones, and families impacted by HD. The chapter also references the University of Utah as an HDSA Center of Excellence. Group dates and locations can change.

**Important Information to Know**
HDSA chapter support and social-worker/resource information do not replace medical, legal, or genetic counseling. Confirm current support-group schedule, clinic referral requirements, and privacy considerations before sharing genetic or health information.
resources.name: HDSA Utah Chapter and University of Utah HD Care Pathway

resources.description: Donated Dental Services program providing donated comprehensive dental treatment through volunteer dentists for eligible Utah applicants who cannot afford care and are 65+, permanently disabled, or need medically necessary dental care.
resources.hours: Application access is online/mail; coordinator hours were not posted on the reviewed page.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must have no means to afford dental care and meet one criterion: over age 65, permanently disabled, or need medically necessary dental care. The program does not provide emergency or cosmetic treatment. Source: https://dentallifeline.org/utah/

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Utah DDS page, download/mail an application, upload additional documents as requested, or contact Utah DLN Coordinator Brandon Leviton at 801-499-6504 or bleviton@DentalLifeline.org. Source: https://dentallifeline.org/utah/

**Access**
Dental Lifeline Network lists all Utah counties as open to new applications. Treatment is provided by volunteer Utah dentists when an applicant is accepted and matched; the administrative office is in Denver.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is not emergency dental care and not every applicant is accepted. Wait times can be long, documentation may be required, and medically necessary cases/veteran instructions may have special application rules. Confirm current county status and expected wait before relying on treatment.
resources.name: Dental Lifeline Network Utah - Donated Dental Services

USDB's hearing PIP services are for deaf and hard-of-hearing children, with eligibility determined through a hearing diagnosis. The program works with Utah Baby Watch Early Intervention. Vision-related PIP/referral details should be confirmed with USDB/Baby Watch for blind or visually impaired children. For Salt Lake County Baby Watch routing, contact USDB Parent Infant Programs at 801-629-4749 or 801-629-4743, or work through local Baby Watch providers listed for Salt Lake County. Source: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/oec/early-childhood-utah-resources/

PIP services are offered throughout Utah. USDB says PIP specialists are members of each Early Intervention team, visits are home-based in natural settings, and frequency is based on the child's IFSP and individual needs. Source: https://www.usdb.org/deaf-school/early-childhoodbirth-to-age-3

**Important Information to Know**
USDB says Deaf and Hard of Hearing services through USDB are free and include ASL and Listening and Spoken Language options, PIP groups, ASL resources, statewide activities, and story time. Confirm referral steps, diagnosis documentation, and whether the hearing or vision PIP team is the correct route.
resources.name: Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind - Parent Infant Program

People First of Utah is a self-advocacy group by people with disabilities for people with disabilities. The page does not list formal documentation requirements to get involved. Source: https://uddc.utah.gov/get-involved/training-and-education/people-first-of-utah/

Call 801-245-7350 or email mcaldwell@utah.gov to ask about current People First groups, Salt Lake County meetings, accessibility, and how to participate. Source: https://uddc.utah.gov/get-involved/training-and-education/people-first-of-utah/

People First is statewide through the Utah Developmental Disabilities Council. Meeting locations, virtual options, and schedules must be confirmed because the public page does not list current local times.

This is self-advocacy, leadership, and peer education. It is not case management, personal care, benefits enrollment, legal representation, or emergency support.
resources.name: Utah Developmental Disabilities Council - People First of Utah

resources.description: Free statewide mental illness peer support, family support groups, education classes, resources, advocacy, and helpline-style information for individuals, families, and caregivers.

resources.informationText:

NAMI Utah serves individuals living with mental illness and their families/caregivers. Public pages do not list diagnosis documentation requirements for support groups or education resources. Source: https://namiut.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-323-9900, email information@namiut.org, or use the NAMI Utah support group, education, and HelpLine/resource links to find current groups and classes. Source: https://namiut.org/

**Access**
NAMI Utah lists support groups, classes, and resources throughout Utah, with a Salt Lake City office. Group locations, virtual options, registration, and schedules change and should be confirmed before attending.

NAMI is not a clinical treatment provider and is not a crisis provider. The site directs anyone struggling or in crisis to call/text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org. Peer support and education can complement, but not replace, professional care.
resources.name: NAMI Utah - Peer Support, Family Support, and Education

resources.description: National nonprofit placing trained service dogs, hearing/task assistance, skilled companions, facility dogs, medical alert dogs, and veteran service dogs at no cost to qualified recipients, with Utah served by the Southwest region.
resources.hours: Application and team-training schedules vary; regional office hours were not confirmed on reviewed pages.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Canine Companions places dogs with adults and children with disabilities, facility professionals serving clients with special needs, veterans with disabilities including PTSD-related tasks, and certain medical-alert needs. Applicants must meet program-specific eligibility, care, travel/training, and matching requirements. Source: https://canine.org/service-dogs/our-dogs/

**How to Best Connect**
Start with Canine Companions' application information on its official site or call 1-800-572-2275. Utah applicants should ask which regional center handles them, current wait times, required travel, documentation, and whether their disability-related tasks match a Canine Companions dog. Source: https://canine.org/service-dogs/our-dogs/

**Access**
Canine Companions serves nationally through regional training centers; Utah is served through the Southwest region. Applicants generally must complete a multi-step application and, if matched, attend team training at the assigned regional center.

**Important Information to Know**
Dogs are provided at no cost, but acceptance and matching are not guaranteed, wait times can be long, and recipients are responsible for ongoing dog care and program requirements. Confirm current regional process, travel/lodging expectations, and whether the organization trains for the needed tasks.
resources.name: Canine Companions - Service Dogs and Assistance Dogs

Amputee Coalition support services are for people with limb loss or limb difference, family members, caregivers, and professionals seeking information/support. Call 888-267-5669, use the online Get Assistance/contact form, email peersupport@amputee-coalition.org for Certified Peer Visitors, email supportgroup@amputee-coalition.org for support-group network help, or connect with a Healthcare Navigator through the support-services page. Sources: https://amputee-coalition.org/contact-us/ and https://amputee-coalition.org/service/find-support-services/

Services are national and remote, available to Salt Lake County residents. The contact page lists office hours as Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Eastern. Virtual groups and peer visits may require registration and depend on volunteer availability.

Healthcare Navigators can help with insurance coverage/appeals, communicating with care teams, prosthetic/orthotic/DME understanding, local resources, and accessibility accommodations. resources.name: Amputee Coalition - Support Services and National Limb Loss Resource Center

Call Jordan Valley School at 801-826-7200 and ask about special education placement, IEP team referral, early childhood contact, transportation, and current program capacity. This is a school placement, not a public drop-in disability center. Admission and services depend on district residency/placement rules, IEP team decisions, evaluations, staffing, and capacity.
resources.name: Canyons School District - Jordan Valley School

resources.description: University of Utah Health outpatient speech-language-hearing clinic providing audiology evaluation/treatment, hearing aids/cochlear implant services, speech-language evaluations and therapy, AAC, aural rehabilitation, voice, stuttering, aphasia, and Parkinson's speech therapy.
resources.hours: Appointments are scheduled; clinic hours were not posted on the reviewed page.
resources.informationText:

The clinic serves children and adults with hearing, speech, language, developmental, and acquired neurological communication disorders. It treats people with developmental disabilities such as autism, Down syndrome, and cerebral palsy, and neurological disorders such as aphasia, traumatic brain injury, ALS, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease. Source: https://healthcare.utah.edu/speech-language-hearing-clinic

Call 801-581-3506 to schedule. For audiology services email hearing@utah.edu; for speech-language services email speechpath@utah.edu. Source: https://healthcare.utah.edu/speech-language-hearing-clinic

The clinic is an outpatient University of Utah Health clinic serving the greater Salt Lake City community. Services are by appointment. The clinic also serves as a graduate training program; services are provided by graduate student clinicians under direct supervision of licensed clinical faculty providers.

**Important Information to Know**
Fees, insurance acceptance, sliding-scale options, and wait times were not confirmed on the reviewed page. The clinic provides evaluation and treatment, not school IEP placement or emergency care. Ask about costs, referrals, telehealth, and expected clinician model when scheduling.
resources.name: University of Utah Health - Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic

resources.description: MDA Care Center pathway at University of Utah Health for adults and children with muscular dystrophy, ALS, spinal muscular atrophy, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, and other neuromuscular disorders.
resources.hours: Clinical Neurosciences Center location posts Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; pediatric clinic hours were not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
People with suspected or diagnosed neuromuscular disorders may seek MDA Care Center services; University of Utah states the clinic treats adults and children with 40+ neuromuscular disorders. Referral, insurance, and appointment availability should be confirmed with the clinic. Sources: https://www.mda.org/care/mda-care-centers and https://healthcare.utah.edu/neurosciences/neurology/muscular-dystrophy-clinic

**How to Best Connect**
Call the adult University of Utah muscular dystrophy clinic at 801-585-7575. For pediatric MDA care listed by MDA, call 801-587-0462. MDA also offers Resource Center support through https://www.mda.org/care/mda-resource-center.

**Access**
Adult care is listed at the Clinical Neurosciences Center, 175 N. Medical Drive East, 4th Floor, Salt Lake City; that location posts Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Pediatric care is listed by MDA at 81 N. Mario Capecchi Dr., Floor 3, Salt Lake City. Confirm referral requirements, clinic schedule, and insurance before relying on a visit.

**Important Information to Know**
MDA Care Centers provide multidisciplinary neuromuscular care and connection to MDA/community resources, not guaranteed financial coverage. Costs, insurance acceptance, wait times, and clinical-trial availability vary by patient and clinic.
resources.name: MDA and University of Utah Health - MDA Care Centers

resources.description: No-cost MDA Summer Camp for eligible youth with neuromuscular disease, with in-person and virtual sessions offered seasonally.
resources.hours: Seasonal camp sessions; application windows and session schedules vary by year.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
MDA Summer Camp is for children and young adults ages 8-17 diagnosed with a neuromuscular disease. Campers may participate in one session each year, selecting an in-person or virtual session that fits their needs. Source: https://www.mda.org/summer-camp

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Camper Information and in-person/virtual camp links on the MDA Summer Camp page, or contact MDA's Resource Center through https://www.mda.org/care/mda-resource-center for help navigating registration.

**Access**
Camp is seasonal. MDA states both in-person and virtual sessions are available each summer, but locations, dates, deadlines, and space vary. Utah families may need to travel for an in-person regional session.

**Important Information to Know**
MDA states camp is provided at no cost to families. Camp includes volunteer health professionals and trained camp volunteers, but acceptance is not guaranteed and medical needs must be reviewed through the camp process.
resources.name: Muscular Dystrophy Association - MDA Summer Camp

Neighborhood House serves adults age 18 and older, including people with developmental disabilities, dementia, cognitive impairments, physical disabilities, chronic conditions, or aging-related support needs. resources.informationText:

The PTI Project supports Utah families of children and young adults with disabilities, plus educators and service providers. It focuses on special education, disability services, rights, advocacy skills, and family-professional partnerships. Sources: https://utahparentcenter.org/program/pti/ and https://utahparentcenter.org/contact-us/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-272-1051 or 800-468-1160, email info@utahparentcenter.org, or use the Utah Parent Center contact form to connect with a parent consultant or training.

Support is statewide and provided primarily by phone, email, trainings, and workshops; in-person office access is at 5296 S Commerce Drive, Suite 302, Murray. Posted phone/email hours are Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, and in-person office hours are Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.

resources.name: Utah Parent Center - Parent Training and Information Project

resources.description: Utah Medicaid HCBS Physical Disabilities Waiver for eligible adults with significant physical disabilities who need personal assistance to remain in home or community settings.
resources.hours: State office hours were not confirmed; call DSPD for current intake hours.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah Medicaid states the Physical Disabilities Waiver is for adults 18+ with physician-certified physical disability, functional loss of two or more limbs, at least 14 hours per week of personal assistance need, ability to direct attendants and manage finances/legal matters, nursing-facility level of care, Medicaid financial eligibility, and an available trained attendant. Source: https://medicaid.utah.gov/ltc-2/pd/

**How to Best Connect**
Contact DSPD at 801-538-4200 to ask about referral, waiting list status, Medicaid financial screening, and waiver application steps.

**Access**
The waiver is statewide and designed to help people remain in their homes or other community settings. Services listed include financial management, personal assistance, personal emergency response, and specialized medical equipment/supplies.

**Important Information to Know**
The waiver serves a limited number of people and has a waiting list. Services are provided only if assessed as needed, and Medicaid/clinical approval is not guaranteed.

resources.description: Utah's statewide Baby Watch Early Intervention Program providing referral, free evaluation access, family coaching, and local Part C early intervention services for infants and toddlers with delays or disabilities.
resources.hours: Baby Watch state office Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; local contractor hours may vary.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Parents, guardians, or professionals concerned about an infant or toddler's development can refer to early intervention. Baby Watch supports infants and toddlers with developmental delays or disabilities; local evaluation determines eligibility. Source: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/oec/baby-watch-early-intervention/

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the local early intervention program for a free evaluation. For Salt Lake County, DHHS lists DDI Vantage for Granite, Murray, and Salt Lake school districts at 801-266-3939, and Jordan Child Development Center for Jordan and Canyons school districts at 801-567-8510. State Baby Watch: 801-273-2900 or 800-961-4226.

**Access**
Services use a family-coaching model in the child's natural environment, such as home or child care. The state Baby Watch office posts Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; local program schedules vary.

**Important Information to Know**
Evaluation is free. Ongoing eligible services may involve Baby Watch family fees or billing; the state page links a family fee form and sliding fee scale. Confirm costs, IFSP services, and local provider assignment before relying on a start date.
resources.name: Utah DHHS - Baby Watch Early Intervention Program

The Alternatives Program is listed for adults age 18+ who can complete a phone intake reviewing ability to perform activities of daily living. Call Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Home & Community Based Care at 385-468-3200 and ask for TAP screening/intake.

The program serves Salt Lake County and begins with phone intake. Services may include case management and coordination of in-home supports for people needing help with tasks such as shopping, meal preparation, transfers, dressing, or medication management.

**Important Information to Know**
Eligibility criteria vary by program and include age, medical condition, and finances. TAP is separate from Medicaid Aging Waiver and Veteran Directed Care; approval, service level, and provider availability are not guaranteed.

resources.informationText:

Current Utah Medicaid materials list Personal Care as a covered Medicaid benefit, and EVV guidance lists personal care service codes. A member must be Medicaid-eligible and meet medical-necessity/provider-manual criteria; exact current criteria and physician order requirements should be confirmed with Utah Medicaid or the member's health plan. **How to Best Connect**
Medicaid applicants can contact DWS eligibility at 866-435-7414. Existing Medicaid members should contact their health plan, Health Program Representative, or Medicaid provider to ask how to request Personal Care Services and prior authorization if needed.

Services are statewide and delivered by Medicaid-enrolled providers in home/community settings when approved. Electronic Visit Verification is required for personal care services.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency caregiver program and not a guaranteed benefit without Medicaid eligibility, provider acceptance, and authorization. The consumer-facing page is limited, so confirm current medical criteria, covered tasks, hours, and provider availability before relying on the service.

resources.hours: Office hours were not published on the page; call before sending or visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
OPG serves adults unable to make basic life decisions due to conditions such as aging-related illness, intellectual disabilities, brain injuries, or mental illness, often when no family or friends can care for them or abuse/neglect/exploitation is involved. Eligibility and service priority criteria apply. Source: https://daas.utah.gov/office-of-public-guardian/

**How to Best Connect**
Follow the OPG referral instructions and submit the referral form by email, mail to 288 N 1460 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116, or fax to 801-538-8243. Call 801-538-8255 with questions.

**Access**
This is a statewide DHHS program with a Salt Lake City office. Referral is document-based rather than walk-in immediate service.

**Important Information to Know**
OPG cannot accept every referral and continues efforts to locate/reunite individuals with family or close friends when appropriate. Guardianship/conservatorship is a legal decision-making pathway; legal advice should come from a qualified attorney or court resource.

resources.description: Utah EHDI newborn hearing-screening, CMV-testing, diagnostic audiology follow-up, early-intervention referral, and parent-to-parent support pathway for infants who are deaf or hard of hearing.
resources.hours: Program office hours were not confirmed; newborn screening and follow-up timelines are time-sensitive.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
EHDI applies to Utah newborns and infants needing hearing screening, repeat screening, diagnostic evaluation, CMV testing after failed screening, and early intervention referral when deaf or hard of hearing. Source: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/cshcn/ehdi/

**How to Best Connect**
Parents should work with the birth facility, pediatrician, pediatric audiologist, and Utah EHDI Program. Contact Utah EHDI at 801-273-6600 when guidance is needed, especially if CMV testing timelines or follow-up are uncertain.

**Access**
Utah goals include screening before hospital discharge or before 10 days of age for out-of-hospital births, repeat screening before 10 days if failed, diagnostic hearing evaluation before 3 months after a second failed screen, CMV testing before 21 days, and early intervention enrollment before 6 months if diagnosed.

**Important Information to Know**
EHDI is a screening, follow-up, referral, and care-coordination system, not a hearing-aid payer. Time-sensitive CMV testing and pediatric audiology follow-up should not be delayed.
resources.name: Utah DHHS - Early Hearing Detection and Intervention

DSPD states caregiver compensation is an ongoing supported living service for people receiving DSPD services, allowing parents, step-parents, legal guardians, and spouses to be paid caregivers for individuals who qualify for living support. Source: https://dspd.utah.gov/caregiver-compensation/

Current DSPD participants should talk with their DSPD support coordinator/provider about caregiver compensation, required family training, forms, certifications, and model options.

The DSPD page provides required training materials, knowledge-check instructions, medical/behavioral certification forms, monthly summary forms, and program guidance. Access is through the existing DSPD service plan rather than general public enrollment.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not available to all families of people with disabilities. It is limited to people already receiving qualifying DSPD living-support services, and hours/compensation depend on assessed need and program rules.

resources.informationText:

UDVMA assists Utah veterans, service members, and eligible family members with VA benefits and claims. Disability compensation and pension outcomes depend on federal VA eligibility and evidence. Source: https://veterans.utah.gov/

**How to Best Connect**
Use the VA Claims Assistance scheduling link on the UDVMA site or call 801-326-2372 to connect with an accredited claims representative.

**Access**
The program is statewide and appointment-based. UDVMA states trained and accredited veteran service officers help prepare, submit, and appeal VA claims free of charge.

This is claims navigation, not emergency aid or a guarantee of VA approval. Ask what records to bring, including DD-214, medical evidence, prior VA letters, and identification.

resources.description: No-cost Head Start and Early Head Start inclusive preschool and early-childhood services for Salt Lake and Tooele County children, with disability-inclusive eligibility and classroom supports.
resources.hours: Center/classroom schedules vary; enrollment office hours were not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah Community Action Head Start/Early Head Start accepts applications for children ages 0-5 and prenatal services. Families at or below 100% of federal poverty level are eligible, and children with disabilities or foster children may still be eligible above poverty guidelines. Source: https://utahca.org/head-start-preschool/

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Utah Community Action Head Start page in English or Spanish, then schedule the eligibility interview/phone appointment. For questions, call 801-359-2444.

**Access**
The program serves Salt Lake and Tooele Counties at multiple centers. It provides no-cost preschool/early childhood education, meals, health/dental/vision/hearing and developmental screenings, family support, and inclusive classrooms. UCA states it does not provide transportation but may assist with carpooling or bus/TRAX vouchers.

**Important Information to Know**
Utah Community Action states 10% of Head Start enrollment is reserved for children with disabilities and placement is not denied based on disability or severity. Classroom availability varies, and application/interview completion does not guarantee immediate placement.
resources.name: Utah Community Action - Inclusive Head Start and Early Head Start

resources.name: National MS Society - MS Navigator and Salt Lake City MS Support Group

This is a clinical rehabilitation/admission-based provider, not an open community drop-in. Costs and access depend on payer authorization, medical necessity, and available placement.

resources.hours: Program hours were not published; call or email before a visit.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Adaptive Care Program is for individuals older than 3 who have a developmental disability and difficulty coping or cooperating in a medical setting beyond what is age appropriate. Source: https://intermountainhealthcare.org/childrens-health/support-services/child-life-services/adaptive-care

Call the Adaptive Care main line at 385-531-4168 or email the program through the address on the Intermountain page. Campus support numbers are 801-664-1290 for Primary Children's Salt Lake and 385-395-1593 for Lehi.

**Access**
Adaptive Care child life specialists create a care plan with families and share it with medical staff throughout Intermountain Health. Supports may include social stories, tours, avoiding crowded areas, communication supports, sensory supports, play/distraction, and exam/treatment support.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an accommodation/support program within Intermountain Children's Health, not a standalone therapy, home-care, or community personal-care benefit. Confirm eligibility, location coverage, and how the plan will be used before appointments.
resources.name: Intermountain Primary Children's Hospital - Adaptive Care Program

resources.description: University Developmental Assessment Clinics multidisciplinary developmental assessment, therapy, and ongoing care for infants, children, and teens with developmental disabilities or developmental concerns.
resources.hours: Clinic hours were not published on the page; appointments/referrals required.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
UDAC evaluates infants, children, and teens with developmental disabilities or developmental concerns and provides developmental assessments, therapy, and ongoing care through child developmental, neuromotor, neonatal follow-up, and heart center neurodevelopment programs. Source: https://healthcare.utah.edu/pediatrics/programs-services/udac

**How to Best Connect**
Use the referral links on the UDAC page for the Child Development Program or Neonatal Follow-Up Program, or call University of Utah Health/Primary Children's pediatric specialty access to confirm the correct referral route.

**Access**
In-person visits are at Primary Children's Eccles Outpatient Services, Level 2, Station 4, 81 N Mario Capecchi Dr., Salt Lake City. Referral, insurance/Medicaid acceptance, wait time, and clinic fit vary by program. UDAC can help establish developmental needs and care recommendations but does not guarantee school, Medicaid, DSPD, or other benefits.
resources.name: University of Utah Health and Primary Children's - University Developmental Assessment Clinics

navigationResources.description: Utah All Means All certified inclusive child-care program directory and Child Care Resource Agency contact route for families seeking licensed child care prepared to include children with disabilities or special needs.
navigationResources.hours: Directory is online anytime; USU Child Care Resource Agency public page does not post office hours, so call before relying on live assistance.
navigationResources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Families do not need a disability-service eligibility determination to use the All Means All certified child-care program list. Individual child-care providers set their own enrollment rules, age ranges, tuition, documentation, and accommodation processes. Source: https://www.usu.edu/childcarehelp/all-means-all-childcare-programs-in-utah

**How to Best Connect**
Use the All Means All certified program list to identify programs in Salt Lake County and click a facility name for provider contact information. For CCR&R help, contact USU Child Care Resource Agency at childcare.help@usu.edu, 435-797-1552, or toll-free 800-670-1552. Sources: https://www.usu.edu/childcarehelp/all-means-all and https://www.usu.edu/childcarehelp/all-means-all-childcare-programs-in-utah

**Access**
The directory lists statewide certified inclusive child-care programs, including multiple Salt Lake County sites. The administrative office is in Logan; families should contact the listed child-care provider directly for openings, hours, location, and enrollment steps.

**Important Information to Know**
All Means All does not appear to pay for child care or guarantee a slot. Provider tuition, subsidy acceptance, transportation, accommodations, staffing, and fit for a child's needs must be confirmed directly with each program.
navigationResources.name: Utah State University Child Care Resource Agency - All Means All Inclusive Child Care
